label: requires server role
type: subject = a SQL++ statement, REST endpoint or UI action; object = a role: concept from Couchbase Server's own 56-member RBAC catalogue (learn/security/roles.md); means the subject is refused unless the authenticated user holds that role. This is the THIRD structurally distinct 'requires a role' predicate in the registry and the three must not be interchanged: requiresRole is Sync Gateway's sync-function requireRole() check (a per-write assertion inside a JavaScript function), requiresCapellaRole takes a capella-role:* management-plane role, and this one takes a Server RBAC role. Distinct from requiresPrivilege, whose object is a real privilege - which, in this corpus, means a Capella privilege:capella-*-access-* id, because Server's catalogue has no separately enumerable privilege tier.
note:
ROUND 13 CORRECTION. This record was minted in round 12 with `recurrence: 20`, and no extraction record used the predicate at all - the 20 counted the files that *should* have used it. Every other recurrence figure in the registry means 'distinct files that use this term', so this one silently meant something else, and read as the best-evidenced new predicate of its round while having zero users. Round 13 rewrote the predicate in the records, via normalise-ids.py, and the figure above is now a real count: 43 files, 76 occurrences.

The underlying reason round 12 left it at zero is worth keeping, because it is a limit of the alias mechanism rather than an oversight. Round 12 fixed the category error by re-filing the eleven concepts and recording their old ids as aliases - which works, and is forward-only - but an alias maps one id to another and so can only ever repair an object, never a predicate. `requiresPrivilege` could not be aliased to `requiresServerRole` because 48 files still use it correctly for Capella's genuinely separate privilege catalogue. So the concept half was repairable additively and the predicate half was not, and the round did the half it could. Round 13 found 38 `requiresPrivilege` occurrences whose object resolved to a role, plus 38 more under `requiresRole` - a predicate that is Sync Gateway's `requireRole()` check and that round 12's sweep never looked at, because it keyed on the *other* predicate name and on `privilege:*` object ids. Those 18 files had neither, and fell between the two sieves.

After the rewrite, `requiresRole` is down to 5 occurrences in 3 files: the two sync-gateway/ records that mean the Sync Gateway thing, and three assertions in transactions.json whose objects are role *categories* rather than roles, which this predicate's range does not admit. See reconciliation.md round 13.

Original round-12 note follows. Minted in round 12 as the necessary other half of the privilege-to-role re-filing. 20 extraction files across the server/7.2, server/8.0 and cloud/ trees assert requiresPrivilege with an object that roles.md documents as a role, so the predicate was carrying the same category error as the concept ids it pointed at - fixing the objects alone would have left a predicate whose declared range is a privilege pointing at eleven roles. requiresPrivilege is kept and is still correct for its ~35 genuine Capella-privilege objects; only the Server-role objects move. Five of the 20 files are cloud/ pages citing Server role names, which is unadapted shared SQL++ reference content rather than a Capella access model - see docs-issues/cloud-sqlpp-pages-cite-server-rbac-roles.
